name: Dissimilatory Sulfate Reduction
notes: Dissimilatory sulfate reduction to sulfide (H2S); key souring mechanism in oil & gas systems. Requires adenylysulfate reductase (aprAB; K00394, K00395) and dissimilatory sulfite reductase (dsrAB; HMM@dsrA, HMM@dsrB).

name: Thiosulfate Reduction (Respiratory)
notes: Respiratory thiosulfate reduction via the PhsABC thiosulfate reductase complex (phsA K08352, phsB K08353, phsC K08354). Requires at least 2 of 3 subunits to account for incomplete genome recovery in metagenomic data. Uses thiosulfate as terminal electron acceptor under anaerobic conditions. Found in Salmonella, Citrobacter, and diverse anaerobes.

name: Thiosulfate Reduction (Rhodanese)
notes: Thiosulfate sulfurtransferase (rhodanese; K01011 rdl/glpE-type, K14180 mitochondrial-type) transfers sulfur from thiosulfate to cyanide or other acceptors, producing sulfite and thiocyanate. Also involved in sulfur relay and cyanide detoxification. Distinct from respiratory thiosulfate reduction — does not conserve energy via electron transport. Extremely widespread across bacteria and archaea so interpret cautiously; presence alone is not diagnostic of dedicated thiosulfate metabolism.

name: Sulfur Oxidation - SOX
notes: Oxidation of reduced sulfur compounds via the SOX multienzyme complex. SoxXA (K17223, K17222) initiate sulfur binding, SoxYZ (K17226, K17227) are the sulfur-carrying proteins, and SoxB (K17224) is the sulfate-releasing thiohydrolase. SoxCD (K17225, K22622) are optional and indicate complete oxidation to sulfate without intermediates.

name: Sulfur Oxidation - Reverse dsr
notes: Oxidation of stored sulfur globules via reverse-running DsrAB, distinguished from reductive DsrAB by co-occurrence with dsrL (K27196), an NADH-dependent oxidoreductase found exclusively in sulfur-oxidizing organisms. Both dsrA/dsrB (K11180/K11181) and dsrL (K27196) required. Found in Chlorobi, some Gammaproteobacteria, and Chromatiales.

name: Tetrathionate Reduction
notes: Tetrathionate reduction via the ttrABC system (ttrA K08359, ttrB K08358, ttrC K08357). At least 2 of 3 subunits required. Relevant as an alternative electron acceptor in anaerobic subsurface and industrial systems.

name: Sulfur Disproportionation
notes: Disproportionation of elemental sulfur or thiosulfate to sulfate and sulfide simultaneously. Requires ATP sulfurylase (K00958), adenylyl-sulfate reductase (K00394 or K00395), and sulfite reductase (K11180 or K11181).

name: Hydrogenotrophic Methanogenesis
notes: Methanogenesis from H2/CO2; dominant pathway in shale and anaerobic digesters. Requires McrA plus hydrogenotrophic pathway genes including F420-reducing hydrogenase subunits and methyl-CoM reductase components.

name: Acetoclastic Methanogenesis
notes: Methanogenesis from acetate; requires McrA, ACS/CODH complex (K00193, K00194, K00197, K00198), and acetate activation via phosphotransacetylase-acetate kinase (K00925, K00625) or acetyl-CoA synthetase (K01895). Taxonomy filter recommended (Methanosarcina or Methanotrichaceae).

name: Methylotrophic Methanogenesis
notes: Methanogenesis from methylated substrates (methanol, methylamines, DMSP); McrA plus methyltransferase homologs (K04480, K14083, K16176, K16178, K25220, K16954, K25600, K25916, K26847).

name: Anaerobic Methane Oxidation (ANME)
rule: HMM@McrA & [tax(g__Methanocomedens_A) | tax(g__Methanocomedens_B) | tax(g__Methanogaster_A) | tax(g__Methanogaster_B) | tax(g__Methanoperedens_A) | tax(g__Methanoperedens) | tax(g__ANME-1-THS) | tax(g__ANME1a) | tax(g__G60ANME1) | tax(g__Methanophaga) | tax(g__Methanovorans) | tax(g__Methanomarinus) | tax(g__Methanoxibalbensis) | tax(g__Methanospirare)]
notes: Anaerobic oxidation of methane by ANME archaea; requires McrA with mandatory taxonomic filter for ANME genera. Taxonomy is essential to distinguish ANME from methanogens which share McrA.

name: Aerobic Methane Oxidation
rule: HMM@pmoa_actinobacteria_chloroflexota | HMM@pmoa_alpha_1 | HMM@pmoa_alpha_2 | HMM@pmoa_crenothrix | HMM@pmoa_gamma | HMM@pmoa_methyl_eth | HMM@pmoa_methylomirabilis | HMM@pmoa_verr
notes: Aerobic oxidation of methane via particulate methane monooxygenase (pMMO); HMMs cover diverse methanotroph lineages including Alphaproteobacteria, Gammaproteobacteria, NC10, Verrucomicrobia, and Actinobacteria. Relevant in oxic zones of engineered systems receiving methane inputs.

name: Fermentative H2 (FeFe)
notes: FeFe hydrogenases; primarily fermentative H2 production across all subgroups. Group A is the most common fermentative H2-producing hydrogenase; Group B is electron-bifurcating; Group C is putatively sensory; Groups E and F are found in anaerobic fungi and diverse anaerobes. All subgroups associated with anaerobic fermentative metabolism.

name: H2 Metabolism - NiFe Group 1
notes: NiFe group 1 hydrogenases; membrane-bound, predominantly H2 uptake linked to respiratory electron transport chain. Most characterized members are H2-consuming; functional inference for uncharacterized members is based on phylogeny. Key for cathodic depolarization MIC and energy conservation in H2-rich systems including underground hydrogen storage.

name: H2 Metabolism - NiFe Group 2
notes: NiFe group 2 hydrogenases; putative sensory/regulatory function detecting environmental H2 concentrations and regulating expression of other hydrogenases. Do not contribute directly to energy conservation. Functional characterization is limited relative to other NiFe groups.

name: H2 Metabolism - NiFe Group 3
notes: Cytoplasmic bidirectional NiFe hydrogenases capable of both H2 production and consumption depending on prevailing redox conditions. Involved in NADH and ferredoxin redox balancing during fermentation and anaerobic metabolism. The bidirectional nature means functional direction cannot be inferred from gene presence alone and is condition-dependent.

name: H2 Metabolism - NiFe Group 4
notes: Membrane-bound energy-conserving NiFe hydrogenases primarily involved in H2 evolution, coupled to ion pumping for energy conservation under anaerobic conditions. Found in strict anaerobes, acetogens, and methanogens. Relevant in anaerobic digesters, shale systems, and underground hydrogen storage where H2 production by microbial communities affects system chemistry and storage integrity.

name: Ammonia Oxidation to Nitrite (Nitrification)
rule: [K28504 | K10945 | K10946 | HMM@amoa_beta | HMM@amoa_gamma | HMM@amoa_crenarchaea] & K10535
notes: Aerobic oxidation of ammonia to nitrite; first step of canonical two-step nitrification. Requires ammonia monooxygenase (amoA; K28504, K10945, K10946, or AmoA HMMs for beta/gammaproteobacterial and archaeal AOB) plus hydroxylamine oxidoreductase (hao; K10535). AmoA HMMs provide better phylogenetic resolution than K numbers alone. Excludes comammox Nitrospira which has a distinct AmoA lineage captured separately.
gene_ids: K28504, K10945, K10946, amoa_beta, amoa_gamma, amoa_crenarchaea, K10535

name: Nitrite Oxidation to Nitrate (Nitrification)
notes: Aerobic oxidation of nitrite to nitrate; second step of nitrification via nitrite oxidoreductase (NXR). HMM-based detection is more specific than K number alone due to paralog confusion between NXR and NarGH.

name: Anaerobic Ammonia Oxidation (Anammox)
notes: Anaerobic ammonium oxidation to dinitrogen gas. Requires nitrite reduction to NO (NirS K00368 or NirK K15864), hydrazine synthase complex (hzsA K20932, hzsB K20933, hzsC K20934 — all three required), and hydrazine dehydrogenase (hdh K20935). The HZS complex is essentially unique to anammox Planctomycetes making this a highly specific rule.

name: Complete Ammonia Oxidation (Comammox)
notes: Complete ammonia oxidation to nitrate by a single organism (comammox Nitrospira). Distinguished from canonical nitrification by the phylogenetically distinct comammox AmoA (HMM@amoa_Nitrospira_beta). Also requires nitrite oxidoreductase (nxr; K00370 or K00371) and hydrazine dehydrogenase (K20935) or equivalent. First predicted and confirmed in engineered systems including drinking water distribution systems, wastewater biofilters, and slow sand filters.

name: Nitrate Reduction to Nitrite
notes: First step of denitrification via membrane-bound nitrate reductase (NarGHI; HMM@NarG) or periplasmic nitrate reductase (NapAB; K02567, K02568). Also relevant in produced water injection systems where nitrate is added for souring control.

name: Nitrite Reduction to NO
notes: Second step of denitrification via NirS (cd1-type nitrite reductase; K00368) or NirK (copper-type nitrite reductase; K15864).

name: NO Reduction to N2O
notes: Third step of denitrification via nitric oxide reductase — cNOR (K04561) or qNOR (K15877).

name: N2O Reduction to N2
notes: Final step of complete denitrification via nitrous oxide reductase (nosZ; K00376). Presence indicates complete denitrification capacity. Absence with upstream denitrification genes present indicates N2O-producing incomplete denitrifier.

name: DNRA (NO3 to NH4)
notes: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium via nitrate reductase (NarGH K00370/K00371 or NapAB K02567/K02568) plus nitrite reductase (NrfAB K00362/K00363 or NirBD K03385/K15876). Competes with denitrification for nitrate; retains nitrogen in system rather than releasing N2.

name: Iron/Manganese/Selenium Reduction
rule: [[Fe@MtrA & Fe@MtrB_TIGR03509 & Fe@MtrC_TIGR03507] | Fe@omcF | Fe@omcS | Fe@omcZ | Fe@FmnA | [Fe@ExtA_pcc_cyt | Fe@ExtB_porin | Fe@ExtC_pcc_lp_cyt | Fe@ExtD_pcc_lp_cyt]]
notes: Dissimilatory Fe(III), Mn(IV), and Se(VI) reduction via outer membrane cytochrome systems. The Mtr system (MtrCAB; Fe@MtrA, Fe@MtrB_TIGR03509, Fe@MtrC_TIGR03507) and Omc cytochromes (Fe@omcS, Fe@omcZ, Fe@omcF) are the primary systems in Shewanella and Geobacter respectively. ExtABCD system found in other iron reducers. No unique diagnostic gene distinguishes Fe(III) from Mn(IV) or Se(VI) reduction — the same EET machinery reduces all three. HMMs from DRAM Fe@ database.
gene_ids: MtrA, MtrB_TIGR03509, MtrC_TIGR03507, omcF, omcS, omcZ, FmnA, ExtA_pcc_cyt, ExtB_porin, ExtC_pcc_lp_cyt, ExtD_pcc_lp_cyt

name: Iron Oxidation
notes: Ferrous iron oxidation for energy conservation. Cyc2 (outer membrane cytochrome, broad iron oxidizers; Fe@Cyc2), MtoAB (neutrophilic iron oxidizers; Fe@MtoA & Fe@MtoB), FoxEYZ (acidophilic iron oxidizers; Fe@FoxE & Fe@FoxY & Fe@FoxZ), PioA (photoferrotrophic iron oxidation; Fe@PioA). HMMs from FeGenie database.
gene_ids: Cyc2, PioA, MtoA, MtoB, FoxE, FoxY, FoxZ

name: Arsenate Reduction (Respiratory)
notes: Respiratory arsenate reduction via the ArrAB complex (arrA K08355, arrB K08356); uses As(V) as terminal electron acceptor for anaerobic energy conservation. Distinct from detoxification arsenate reductase (arsC) which reduces As(V) to As(III) solely for efflux. Found in diverse anaerobes including Shewanella, Chrysiogenes, and Sulfurospirillum. Relevant in arsenic-rich subsurface and produced water systems.

name: Arsenite Oxidation
notes: Arsenite oxidase large subunit (aioA/aoxB; K08356) and small subunit (aioB/aoxA; K08355) oxidize As(III) to As(V). Can serve as lithotrophic energy conservation (electrons feed into quinone pool) or as detoxification. Both subunits required. Note: K08355 and K08356 are shared with respiratory arsenate reduction (arrAB) due to KEGG numbering ambiguity — interpret in genomic context.

name: Extracellular Electron Transfer (EMIC)
notes: Direct extracellular electron transfer (EET) from metal surface to microbial cell; primary mechanism of electrical MIC (EMIC). Mtr system (MtrCAB) in Shewanella requires all three subunits; OmcS and OmcZ are outer membrane cytochromes in Geobacter sufficient alone. Overlaps with Fe/Mn reduction rule — interpret in context of biofilm presence and metal surface contact.

name: Iron Acquisition (Ferrous, Feo)
notes: Ferrous iron (Fe2+) uptake via the Feo system. FeoB_N, FeoB_C, FeoB_gate are domains of the same FeoB GTPase-gated membrane channel — any domain detection indicates FeoB presence. FeoA is the small accessory cytoplasmic protein required alongside FeoB. Primary Fe(II) uptake route under anaerobic/microaerobic conditions. HMMs from FeGenie.

name: Iron Acquisition (Ferric, Fbp/Fut)
notes: Ferric iron (Fe3+) ABC transport systems. FbpABC (heterotrophic bacteria; requires at least 2 of 3 subunits for confident call). FutABC (cyanobacteria; requires ATPase FutC plus at least one substrate-binding protein FutA1 or FutA2). Relevant under oxic or iron-limited conditions. HMMs from FeGenie.

name: Arsenic Resistance
notes: Arsenate detoxification via arsenate reductase (arsC; K00537 glutaredoxin-type or K03741 thioredoxin-type) reducing As(V) to As(III), coupled with arsenite export via ArsB (K03893) or Acr3 (K03325) efflux pumps. ArsA ATPase (K01551) and ArsH (K11811) provide additional resistance capacity. Not respiratory — distinct from arrAB respiratory arsenate reduction in Metal Cycling.

name: Arsenic Methylation
notes: Arsenite S-adenosylmethionine methyltransferase (arsM; K07755) detoxifies arsenic via sequential methylation to organoarsenicals (monomethylarsenic, dimethylarsenic, trimethylarsine gas). Distinct detoxification strategy from efflux — volatilizes arsenic. Found in diverse bacteria and archaea including methanogens.

name: Copper Resistance
rule: [copA | K17686 | copB | K01533 | [[cusA-ybdE | K07787] & [cusB | K07798] & [cusC-ylcB | K07796]]] & [cueO | K14588 | mco | K22552 | cusF-cusX | K07810]
notes: Copper efflux via P-type ATPases (copA K17686 Cu+, copB K01533 Cu2+) or CusCBA RND efflux system (K07787, K07798, K07796) combined with periplasmic detoxification via cuproxidase CueO (K14588), multicopper oxidase Mco (K22552), or chaperone CusF (K07810). CopC (K07156) and CopD (K07245) are additional resistance proteins.

rule: [merA | K00520] & [merT | K08363 | merC | K19058 | merE | K19059 | merF]
notes: Mercuric reductase (merA; K00520) reduces ionic Hg(II) to volatile Hg(0) requiring mercury import via MerT (K08363), MerC (K19058), MerE (K19059), or MerF. MerP (K08364) is a periplasmic Hg-binding protein. merB (K00221) additionally cleaves organomercury compounds. merR (K08365) and merD (K19057) are regulatory. Note merF lacks a confirmed K number — included in gene names only.

name: Chromate Resistance
notes: Chromate efflux transporter (chrA; K07240) and chromate resistance protein (chrB; K19784). ChrA actively exports chromate from the cell. Relevant in industrial and mining-influenced systems with chromate contamination.

name: Cadmium/Zinc/Cobalt Resistance
rule: at_least(2, PRESENCE, [czcA | K15726, czcB | K15727, czcC | K15725]) | [zntA-yhhO | K01534] | [zitB-ybgR | K16264]
notes: Heavy metal efflux via CzcABC RND efflux system (K15726/K15727/K15725; at least 2 of 3 subunits required for metagenomic data) handling Cd/Zn/Co, ZntA P-type ATPase (K01534) for Zn/Cd export, or ZitB CDF transporter (K16264). CadX (K21903) and CzrB (K21133) are regulators.

name: Nickel/Cobalt Resistance
notes: Nickel and cobalt efflux via NrsA (K11326), RcnA/NicO family (K08970), CnrY (K24079) and CnrR (K24078) of the CnrYXH/CnrCBA system, or CtpD P-type ATPase (K12951). Relevant in stainless steel corrosion environments and industrial bioreactors where nickel leaches from equipment.

name: Silver Resistance
notes: Silver efflux via SilP P-type ATPase (K23254); SilF and SilE are periplasmic silver-binding proteins. K number only confirmed for silP; silF and silE lack confirmed K numbers. Relevant in engineered systems using silver-based antimicrobials.

name: Lead Resistance
notes: Lead resistance via PbrR transcriptional regulator and PbrT Pb(II) membrane transporter. pbrR and pbrT lack confirmed K numbers in current KEGG — gene name identifiers used. Rule requires HMM development for reliable detection.

name: Acetate Production
notes: Acetate production via multiple fermentative routes: (1) oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA via pyruvate dehydrogenase (K00163, K00161, K00162), pyruvate ferredoxin oxidoreductase (K00174, K00175), or pyruvate formate lyase (K01568), followed by acetate release via acetate kinase/phosphotransacetylase (K01905, K22224, K24012); (2) direct aldehyde oxidation routes (K00138, K00128, K14085, K00149, K00129); or (3) acetyl-CoA hydrolysis (K01895, K01913).

name: Propionate Production
notes: Propionate production via three routes: (1) methylmalonyl-CoA pathway involving succinyl-CoA intermediates (K01899, K01900, K01902, K01903, K01847, K01849, K01848, K00140, K01895, K01908); (2) acrylate pathway via lactate (K01026, K20626, K20627, K00248, K00232); or (3) propionyl-CoA pathway (K01699, K13919, K13920, K13922). Key fermentation product and syntrophic substrate.

name: Butyrate Production
notes: Butyrate production via multiple routes: (1) classical acetyl-CoA condensation pathway (K00626, K00074/K00022, K01692, K00209/K17829, K01034/K01035/K19709); (2) glutarate pathway (K00135/K08324/K00139/K17761, K00043/K08318/K18120/K18121, K18122, K14534); (3) lysine pathway (K01580, K13524/K07250/K14268/K00823/K16871); or (4) 4-aminobutyrate pathway (K01843).

name: Lactate Production
notes: Lactate production via three routes: (1) complete glycolytic route followed by lactate dehydrogenase (K00016); (2) lactate dehydrogenase alone (K00016) as minimal call; or (3) PTS sugar system route (K18124/K18125/K00115/K19813/K00117 & K01053 & K05308 & K11395/K18127 & K00016). Lactate is a primary fermentation product in Firmicutes and relevant as MIC organic acid, SRB substrate, and electron donor.

name: Formate Production
notes: Formate production via pyruvate formate lyase (PFL; K00656) cleaving pyruvate to formate and acetyl-CoA under strictly anaerobic conditions, or via formate dehydrogenase — FDH-N subunits (K00122, K00123; both required) or FDH-H subunits (K00124, K00125, K00126; at least 2 required). Formate is a key interspecies electron/H2 carrier in syntrophic systems.

name: Succinate Production
notes: Succinate production via fumarate reductase — catalytic subunits frdA/frdB (K00244, K00245) plus membrane anchor subunits frdC/frdD (K00246, K00247). Note fumarate reductase is also involved in other metabolisms beyond succinate production; interpret in context of broader fermentative metabolism.

name: Ethanol Production
notes: Ethanol production via pyruvate formate lyase (K01568) plus alcohol dehydrogenase (K00001, K00121, K13953), or via acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (K00128, K00149) coupled with alcohol dehydrogenase (K01895/K04072). Relevant in industrial bioreactors, bioethanol systems, and as carbon source for other organisms in mixed communities.

name: Butanol Production
notes: Butanol production via ABE fermentation pathway; requires butyryl-CoA formation (thiolase K00634 plus butyryl-CoA acetyltransferase K00929 or K01896) followed by reduction to butanol via butanol dehydrogenase (bdh; K00100) or NADH-dependent butanol dehydrogenase (K00544). Butyryl-CoA intermediate shared with butyrate pathway. Found predominantly in Clostridia.

HMMs from CANT-HYD database.

notes: Anaerobic alkane oxidation via fumarate addition (AssA; alkylsuccinate synthase/masD; C3-C12 alkanes) or hydroxylation (AhyA; alkane C2 methylene hydroxylase). HMMs from CANT-HYD. Highly relevant in shale and oil reservoir systems where anaerobic conditions dominate.

notes: Anaerobic PAH degradation via fumarate addition (NmsA; naphthyl-2-methylsuccinate synthase; naphthalene) or carboxylation (K27540; naphthalene carboxylase). HMMs from CANT-HYD.

notes: Glucose utilization via PTS (K02777, K02779, K02791), glucose transporters, and glycolytic entry enzymes (glucokinase K00844, K00845). A positive call is expected in nearly all heterotrophs.

name: Sucrose Use
notes: Sucrose utilization via invertase (K01182, K01203), sucrose phosphorylase (K00690), sucrose-6-phosphate hydrolase (K01193), or PTS-mediated uptake.

name: Mannose Use
notes: Mannose utilization via mannose-6-phosphate isomerase (K01809) or PTS mannose transporter (K02793, K02794, K02795, K02796).

name: Galactose Use
notes: Galactose utilization via galactokinase (K00849), UDP-glucose-hexose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (K00965), UDP-galactose-4-epimerase (K01784), or galactose mutarotase (K01785).

name: Fucose Use
notes: Fucose utilization via L-fucose isomerase (K01818), fuculokinase (K00879), or fuculose-1-phosphate aldolase (K01628).

name: Xylose Use
notes: Xylose utilization via xylose isomerase (K01805), xylulokinase (K00854), or Weimberg/Dahms pathway enzymes. Major hemicellulose-derived sugar.

name: Fructose Use
notes: Fructose utilization via fructokinase (K00847), PTS fructose transporters (K02768-K02771), or fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase.

name: Arabinose Use
notes: Arabinose utilization via L-arabinose isomerase (K01804), ribulokinase (K00011), or related enzymes. Common component of hemicellulose and pectin.

name: Ribose Use
notes: Ribose utilization via ribokinase (K00852).

name: Rhamnose Use
notes: Rhamnose utilization via L-rhamnose isomerase (K01813), rhamnulokinase (K01820), or rhamnulose-1-phosphate aldolase (K18337).

name: Maltose Use
notes: Maltose utilization via maltase (K05343), maltose phosphorylase (K00691), or alpha-glucosidase (K01187, K12047).

name: Trehalose Use
notes: Trehalose utilization via trehalase (K01194), trehalose phosphorylase (K02819), or PTS trehalose transporter. Note trehalose biosynthesis genes (K05342, K05343) overlap with osmoregulation sugar synthesis row — interpret in context.

name: Lactose Use
notes: Lactose utilization via beta-galactosidase (K01190) or PTS lactose transporter (K12111, K12112, K12309). Relevant in wastewater systems receiving dairy effluents.

name: Glycerol Use
notes: Glycerol utilization via glycerol kinase (K00864), glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (K00005, K06120, K06121, K06122), glycerol dehydrogenase (K00002), or glycerol uptake facilitator (K13979). Glycerol is released during lipid hydrolysis and is a fermentation substrate in digesters and bioreactors.

name: Ethylene Glycol Degradation
notes: Ethylene glycol degradation via glycolate oxidase (K11472) or diol dehydratase (K18394) for initial oxidation, followed by alcohol dehydrogenase (K00001, K00121) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (K14085, K00128, K00149). Ethylene glycol is used as antifreeze in pipelines and gas processing facilities. Note: K11472 and K18394 removed per curation.

name: Methanol Use
notes: Methanol oxidation via methanol dehydrogenase: calcium-dependent MDH (mxaF; K14028) in Alphaproteobacterial methylotrophs, lanthanide-dependent MDH (xoxF; K16254) increasingly recognized as broadly distributed, or NAD-dependent MDH (mdh; K00121) with broader phylogenetic distribution. K00121 is less specific — co-occurrence with K14028 or K16254 strengthens the call. Methanol is injected as hydrate inhibitor in oil and gas pipelines and used as denitrification carbon source in wastewater treatment.

name: EPS Production
notes: Exopolysaccharide biosynthesis and biofilm matrix structural genes including alginate biosynthesis (alg genes; K16566, K16557, K16556, K16555), Psl polysaccharide biosynthesis (K19290-K19296), PGA/ICA poly-GlcNAc synthesis (pgaABCD/icaABCD; K11936, K11937), and additional EPS biosynthesis genes. Any single gene indicates EPS production capacity. Drives pipeline fouling and MIC in engineered systems.

name: Quorum Sensing
notes: Quorum sensing via three systems: (1) AHL/LuxI-LuxR: LuxI-type AHL synthases lasI (K13060) or rhlI/cepI/tofI homologs (K13061) paired with LuxR-type receptors lasR (K18304) or rhlR homologs (K18099) — both synthase and receptor required; (2) AI-2/LuxS system: LuxS S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase (K07173) — widely conserved but interpret alone cautiously as it has metabolic roles beyond QS; (3) AI-2 import via Lsr ABC transporter: LsrB substrate-binding (K10555), LsrC permease (K10556), LsrD permease (K10557), LsrA ATPase (K10558) — at least 2 subunits required — indicates active AI-2 uptake and response capacity.

name: Motility
notes: Flagellar motor (MotA K02410 or MotB K02411; at least one required) plus at least 3 structural/assembly genes from the flagellar complex. Required for surface approach and early biofilm attachment. Also relevant for chemotaxis toward carbon/electron donor sources in engineered systems.

name: Salt-In Strategy (K+ Accumulation)
notes: Halophilic salt-in osmoadaptation via K+ accumulation and Na+ exclusion. KdpABC P-type ATPase (K01546-K01548) imports K+; KdpDE (K07646, K07667) sensor-regulator. Mrp/Mnh Na+:H+ antiporter (K05565-K05571; Mrp subunit K05565 required plus at least 3 others). PhaABCDEFG K+ transporter (K05559-K05564; at least 2 of 6). TrkA/TrkH constitutive K+ uptake (K03499 & K03498; both required). NhaC Na+:H+ antiporter (K03315 or K07084). Highly relevant in hypersaline produced waters (TDS >200 g/L).

name: Compatible Solutes: Methylated (Synthesis)
notes: Glycine betaine biosynthesis via two routes: (1) choline oxidation pathway — choline dehydrogenase (betA; K00108 or K11440) AND betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase (betB; K00130); or (2) sequential N-methylation of glycine — glycine/sarcosine methyltransferase (K18896) AND sarcosine/dimethylglycine methyltransferase (K18897).

name: Compatible Solutes: Ectoine (Synthesis)
notes: Ectoine biosynthesis via complete ectABC pathway: diaminobutyrate acetyltransferase (ectA; K06718), diaminobutyrate aminotransferase (ectB; K00836), ectoine synthase (ectC; K06720) — all three required. Ectoine hydroxylase (ectD; K10674) additionally produces hydroxyectoine with enhanced thermostability. Major compatible solute in halophilic bacteria.

name: Compatible Solutes: Sugars (Synthesis)
notes: Biosynthesis of sugar-derived compatible solutes. Trehalose: OtsAB (K00697 & K01087; both required), TreYZ (K06044 or K01236), TreS (K05343), TreP (K05342). Mannosylglycerate: mpgSP (K05947). Mannitol: mtlD (K00009). Note K05342 and K05343 overlap with Trehalose Use row in Carbon Degradation.

name: Compatible Solutes: Methylated (Transport)
notes: Transport of glycine betaine, choline, proline, and related methylated osmoprotectants. BetP/T/S BCCT transporter (K02168), carnitine/betaine antiporter (K05245), OpuD betaine transporter (K05020). ProVWX ABC transporter (K02000 & K02001 & K02002; all three required). OpuABC (K05845, K05846, K05847; at least 2 subunits). Glutamine ABC (K10036, K10037, K10038; at least 2 subunits). ProP MFS transporter (K03762); ProQ effector (K03607).

name: Compatible Solutes: Ectoine (Transport)
notes: Ectoine/hydroxyectoine uptake via EhuABC ABC transporter (EhuA ATPase K02028, EhuC/D permease K02029, EhuB substrate-binding protein K02030). At least 2 of 3 subunits required for metagenomic data. Organisms with transport but not synthesis genes are ectoine scavengers.

name: Compatible Solutes: Sugars (Transport)
notes: Sugar osmoprotectant transport. SmoEF ABC system (K10227-K10230; at least 2 subunits), SrlABE PTS (K02783, K02781, K02782; at least 2 subunits), mannitol PTS (mtlA; K02798). Trehalose: dedicated transporter (K17314) or maltose/trehalose ABC (K10109-K10111; at least 2 subunits). Organisms with transport but not synthesis genes scavenge solutes from environment.

name: Heat Shock Response
notes: Heat shock chaperones and proteases. DnaK (K04043) and DnaJ (K04079) form core chaperone system; GroEL/GroES (K04080, K04081) provide folding assistance; GrpE (K03686) is nucleotide exchange factor; ClpB (K03695) disaggregates protein aggregates; ClpXP (K03687) and HslUV are ATP-dependent proteases for misfolded proteins. Essential for survival in high-temperature wells and geothermal systems.

name: Cold Shock Response
notes: Cold shock response via cold shock proteins (CspA family; K10257) acting as RNA chaperones, RecA (K03704) for SOS response, trigger factor (K02834) as ribosome-associated chaperone, and CsdA/DeaD (K05592) cold-inducible DEAD-box RNA helicase. Relevant in surface-to-subsurface transitions and temperature-fluctuating systems.

name: Beta-Lactam Resistance
notes: Beta-lactamase and penicillin-binding protein resistance genes conferring resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics (penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems). Major antibiotic resistance gene class in environmental microbiomes.

name: Macrolide Resistance
notes: Macrolide resistance via efflux pumps, ribosomal methylases (erm genes), or macrolide esterases.

name: Tetracycline Resistance
notes: Tetracycline resistance via efflux pumps (tet efflux genes) or ribosomal protection proteins.

name: Sulfonamide Resistance
notes: Sulfonamide resistance via dihydropteroate synthase variants (sul1, sul2, sul3) insensitive to sulfonamide inhibition. Among the most commonly detected antibiotic resistance genes in wastewater and water treatment systems.

name: Biocide Efflux (General)
notes: Broad-spectrum efflux genes for biocide and multidrug resistance. MexA/membrane fusion protein (K03585), MATE efflux (K03400), MexB/RND pump (K18138), AcrD/RND pump (K18324), AcrF/RND pump (K18142), and SMR family pumps: Mmr (K03297), EbrA/EbrB paired SMR pump (K11814 & K11815), Ebr SMR pump (K18975). Aldehyde dehydrogenase (K14085) provides chemical detoxification capacity. RND pumps (2.A.6 TCDB family) provide broad substrate efflux relevant in oil and gas and wastewater systems. General row is superset of Aldehyde Resistance sub-row.

name: Aldehyde Resistance
notes: Resistance to aldehyde biocides (e.g., glutaraldehyde, formaldehyde) mediated by aldehyde oxidoreductases and aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases (K00149, K14085), which detoxify reactive aldehyde compounds.

name: QAC Resistance
notes: Resistance to quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) disinfectants mediated by multidrug efflux transporters (K08167, K11741) that export toxic biocides from the cell.

name: Oxidative Stress Resistance
notes: Presence of oxidative stress response genes indicates microbial potential to detoxify reactive oxygen species through catalase–peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, glutathione biosynthesis,  NADH peroxidase, or related genes/proteins, supporting survival under oxidative stress.
